results.summary: The agent had to fix six layout defects in BokehJS that showed up in a video clip: Row/Column border alignment, the wrong grid columns in align_borders, the top align border being ignored in BorderLayout, the order of DOM elements in the left panel, a one-directional has_size_changed comparison, and the flex value given to stretching children. It fixed the align_borders column indices and the BorderLayout top border. It moved align_borders() into the LayoutDOMView base class instead of adding a FlexBox override. It changed has_size_changed from '>' to '<' instead of '!=', so the check still fires in only one direction. It missed the left-panel DOM order bug and the flex '1 0 auto' bug entirely, and it could not render anything because no Chrome was available. The verifier passed 7 of 12 f2p tests and 4 of 5 p2p tests. Its one-directional fix broke the p2p test where tick labels narrow, so the reward was 0.

task_specification.explanation: The instruction is deliberately vague but gives general rules that match what the tests check: labels and controls are shown whole and don't overlap at every moment, the frame keeps its size, rows and columns align, and every chart stays inside its row or column. The clip shows each defect, including the left legend and toolbar overlaps and the stretch_width chart running off the page. The agent failed because of its own limits, not because the spec was missing anything. It missed two defects. It also chose a '<' comparison, which broke shrink relayout, even though the instruction says to keep everything else behaving as it does now.

results.summary: The agent was asked to fix BokehJS layout defects shown in a screen recording (plots in Row/Column/Grid losing axes, cropped frames, overlapping legends and toolbars, side panels not relayouting, stretched charts overflowing). It found and fixed five of the six injected defects: the alignment-border hoisting into measure_layout (moved into LayoutDOMView instead of FlexBoxView), the swapped c0/c1 column indices in alignments.ts, the ignored align_border.top in border.ts, the reversed left-panel DOM order in plot_canvas.ts, and the '>' vs '!=' comparison in side_panel.ts. It glanced at flex_box.ts but never noticed the '1 0 auto' vs '1 0 0px' flex value for stretching children. The verifier passed 11/12 fail-to-pass and 5/5 pass-to-pass tests; the only failure was 'stretching across a row stay within the row' (second chart at [910,1810] outside the row [10,910]), so with a binary reward the trial scored 0.

results.summary: The agent was asked to fix several BokehJS layout bugs shown in a screen recording: plots in rows, columns and grids being cropped or misaligned, and plots not relaying out after their content changes. Its patch touched all five files with injected defects. It fixed the align_borders column-index swap, made BorderLayout respect align_border.top, made SideLayout.has_size_changed fire on growth as well as shrinkage, changed stretching flex children to '1 0 0px', and reversed the order of the left panel's DOM elements. Instead of adding a FlexBoxView override, it moved the align_borders call into LayoutDOMView.measure_layout so every container runs it, and it made an extra change to fixed-size inner width and height in alignments.ts. The verifier passed all 12 f2p and 5 p2p tests, for a reward of 1.0.

results.summary: The agent had to fix several BokehJS layout defects shown in a recording of charts in rows, columns and grids. It extracted frames, rebuilt BokehJS, and found five of the six injected defects: the missing align_borders() call in FlexBoxView.measure_layout, the swapped c0/c1 columns in alignments.ts, the missing align_border.top in border.ts, the left-panel element order in plot_canvas.ts, and the '>' vs '!=' comparison in side_panel.ts. Its fixes match the reference fix. It missed the sixth defect: in flex_box.ts, stretch_width children get flex '1 0 auto' instead of '1 0 0px', so two stretching charts in a Row each take the full row width. The verifier passed 11 of 12 f2p tests and all 5 p2p tests. The stretch test failed ('second chart [910, 1810] is not within the row [10, 910]'), so under binary grading the reward was 0.
